title: Your first batch of liquid soap, tested and scaled
course_title: Detergent and Cleaning Products Production: Liquid Soap, Hand Wash and Safe Cleaning

say: Your first batch of liquid soap, tested and scaled.
This is the video for module two of Detergent and Cleaning Products Production.
Put on goggles, gloves and sleeves, with rinse water ready, and start from a formula you trust.
First, sprinkle nitrosol slowly onto the measured water while stirring. Dumped in, it forms lumps that never dissolve. Let it swell until clear and thick.

say: Acid strength and caustic purity vary between suppliers, so a fixed amount of caustic can be wrong. Below about pH 6, acid remains and the soap will sting hands.

panel.heading: Measure pH, never guess
items: Below about 6: acid remains, stings hands
Well above 9: too much alkali, harsh
Adds a little soda ash in two portions

say: Well above 9 means too much alkali, which is harsh on skin.

say: A full 25-litre batch on your first try is how money gets wasted. Test small first. For example, Halima's trainer gave her a 20-litre formula. One line says 100 ml of perfume.

panel.heading: The one-litre method
items: Test batch: 5 ml x 2 L = 10 ml

say: She divides by 20 to get the amount per litre: 5 ml.

panel.heading: The one-litre method
items: Test batch: 5 ml x 2 L = 10 ml

say: For a 2-litre test batch, 5 times 2 is 10 ml.

panel.heading: The one-litre method
items: Test batch: 5 ml x 2 L = 10 ml

say: For a 25-litre batch, 5 times 25 is 125 ml. She does this for every line, so the test batch truly predicts the big one. And she changes only one thing at a time.

items: Test batch: 5 ml x 2 L = 10 ml

say: Salt thickens SLES products. Dissolve it in water and add a small portion at a time. Stir, wait and check.
Time how many seconds the product takes to run out of the same small cup with a hole. Now thick becomes a number you can repeat.

panel.heading: Salt thickens, then thins
left: Add a small portion, stir, wait
Time a flow test each time
right: Past the peak, it thins again

say: But salt only works up to a peak. Keep adding and the liquid gets thinner again, and you cannot take the salt out. If it gets thinner, stop and note the amount.

say: A test batch is ready to scale when it passes every check two times in a row. pH near neutral. The flow time you want. No lumps.
It removes palm oil from a plate well, and it does not separate after a few days. Then it becomes your master formula.

panel.heading: Pass all checks two times in a row
items: Good grease removal on an oily plate
No separation after a few days

say: Customers will ask for something that kills germs. Your liquid soap is a cleaner, not a disinfectant. Teach them to use household bleach. First, clean the surface with detergent and water.

cards.d: Wash the surface with detergent and water, because dirt protects germs.
For 5% to 9% bleach, roughly 20 ml per litre. Leave at least 1 minute. Follow your label.
Make it fresh daily. Never mix bleach with any other cleaner.

say: For bleach of 5% to 9% strength, the US CDC guidance works out to roughly 20 ml per litre of water, left on for at least 1 minute. Brands differ, so read the label and follow its directions.

cards.d: Wash the surface with detergent and water, because dirt protects germs.
For 5% to 9% bleach, roughly 20 ml per litre. Leave at least 1 minute. Follow your label.
Make it fresh daily. Never mix bleach with any other cleaner.

say: Make it fresh every day, in a labelled container, never a drink bottle. And never mix bleach with your soap or any other cleaner.

For 5% to 9% bleach, roughly 20 ml per litre. Leave at least 1 minute. Follow your label.
Make it fresh daily. Never mix bleach with any other cleaner.

say: So remember. Neutralise in portions and check pH each time. Write formulas per litre. Change one thing at a time. Salt thickens only up to a peak.
Your hand wash will be mostly SLES, near neutral and always preserved. And never claim your detergent kills germs.

panel.heading: Key points
items: Neutralise in portions; check pH each time
Change one thing at a time
Salt thickens up to a peak only
Never claim your soap kills germs
